CAPITAL GAIN TAX EXPLAINED

You buy shares for ₦1,000,000.

Later, you sell them for ₦1,500,000.

Capital gain = ₦1,500,000 − ₦1,000,000 = ₦500,000

If, for illustration, the applicable tax rate on that gain is 25%:

₦500,000 × 25% = ₦125,000 tax

You would be left with:

₦500,000 − ₦125,000 = ₦375,000 profit after tax.

For a company where CGT is usually 30%: 

₦500,000 × 30% = ₦150,000.

The company will be left with ₦350,000

Crypto Taxation in Nigeria: What the NTAA 2025 Means for Your Trading Activity
Nigeria's tax administration entered a new phase on 1 January 2026 when the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA) 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act (NTAA) 2025 took full effect. Can Nigeria Really Tax Your Crypto?
The Nigeria Revenue Service just released guidelines on taxing cryptocurrency and other digital assets, built on the new Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and Tax Administration Act 2025. If you trade crypto, hold USDT, do P2P, or earn from Web3, this affects you.
Here is the simple version. Individuals making profit from crypto, whether from trading, staking, mining, or getting paid in crypto, could owe up to 25% tax on those gains. Businesses dealing in digital assets, like exchanges, face 30% corporate tax on their profits. Exchanges themselves now have to register with NRS, get a Tax ID, and file monthly reports showing customer names and transaction details.
But can government really enforce this, since blockchain is supposedly private? Actually, the opposite is true. Blockchain is public, every transaction is visible forever. What is hidden is who owns the wallet. Nobody knows a wallet belongs to you until something links your name to it.
That link happens on exchanges. The moment you convert naira to crypto or crypto back to naira on a platform like Binance or Quidax, that platform already has your ID and bank details from KYC. So when NRS asks exchanges to report transactions, they are not cracking any code. They are just asking the one party that already knows who you are. This is the same method used in the US, UK, and EU.
Where it gets shaky is P2P trading. When crypto moves wallet to wallet with no exchange in the middle, there is no single company holding your identity on file, so enforcement is much harder there for now.
Bottom line, your crypto stops being anonymous the moment it touches a bank account or a licensed exchange. This guideline just makes that official

Nigeria is set to implement a comprehensive cryptocurrency taxation framework in 2026 under the Nigerian Tax Administration Act (NTAA) 2025. 

This marks a significant shift toward formalizing the country's booming crypto sector by integrating digital assets into the official tax system.
All crypto transactions must now be linked to verified Tax Identification Numbers (TINs) and National Identification Numbers (NINs), ensuring traceability to real-world identities.

Here are the key elements of the new rules:

Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs)  including exchanges and brokers  are required to register with tax authorities, enforce strict KYC procedures, and submit monthly transaction reports.

Providers must maintain detailed customer and transaction records for at least seven years.

Suspicious or large transactions must be reported to the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).
Non-compliance risks severe penalties, including fines up to ₦10 million or license revocation.

Rather than directly monitoring the blockchain, the government will rely on VASPs for oversight  an approach that balances regulation with blockchain integrity while aligning Nigeria with global standards like the OECD’s Crypto Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).

This comes as Nigeria ranks among the world's fastest-growing crypto markets, recording an estimated $92.1 billion in transaction volume between July 2024 and June 2025.

 Even partial taxation could generate significant revenue, helping raise the tax-to-GDP ratio from below 10% to 18% by 2027 and reducing oil dependency

Overall, the 2026 Crypto Tax Law aims to enhance transparency, boost market credibility, encourage formal participation, and drive sustainable growth in Nigeria's digital asset ecosystem while increasing government revenue.
